source: Hy-Line W-80 India Commercial Layers Management Guide, Srinivasa Hy-Line, May 2024 (c) Hy-Line International; 33 numbered pages, PDF file W-80-Management-Guide_compressed.pdf
purpose: Climate and husbandry guidance for the shed autopilot. Not loaded by the standards seed; read by the climate rules.

layingTo100Weeks.shellColourScore: Uniformly white (05-10); first-week eggs typically darker (10-20)

temperatureRecommendationsC.stage: House pre-heat, 24 h before chick placement
temperatureRecommendationsC.note: Air temperature measured at chick level, with 60% humidity. Pre-heat 24 h in normal climates, 48 h in cool climates, 72 h in cold climates.
For every 5 percentage-point increase in relative humidity above 60%, reduce brooding temperature by 1 C. After the first week reduce temperature 2-3 C per week until reaching 21 C.

temperatureRecommendationsC.stage: Rearing / growing house (after brooding, to ~18 weeks)
temperatureRecommendationsC.note: Phase-feeding chart: 18-21 C, only change 1 degree every 2 weeks

temperatureRecommendationsC.stage: At housing in the laying house
temperatureRecommendationsC.note: Increase house temperature about 1 C every 2 weeks until reaching 25 C, provided ventilation can maintain air quality
Air Quality page: production house should be at 18-25 C and 40-60% humidity
Use temperature to control feed consumption and egg size; only change 1 degree every 2 weeks. Lower (colder) temperatures after peak increase feed intake and work against egg-weight control.
Feed and water consumption in the performance tables assume 21-27 C

ventilation: General rule for required fan capacity: 4 m3 of air movement per kilogram of body weight per hour.
Production house should be kept at 18-25 C and 40-60% relative humidity.
Air movement table (m3/hour per 1000 birds) at ambient 32 C: week 1 = 340, week 3 = 510, week 6 = 1020, week 12 = 2550, week 18 = 5950, week 19+ = 4650-9350.
Air movement at ambient 21 C: week 1 = 170, week 3 = 255, week 6 = 510, week 12 = 1275, week 18 = 2550, week 19+ = 4250-5100.
Air movement at ambient 10 C: week 1 = 120, week 3 = 170, week 6 = 340, week 12 = 680, week 18 = 1870, week 19+ = 2550-3400.
Air movement at ambient 0 C: week 1 = 70, week 3 = 130, week 6 = 230, week 12 = 465, week 18 = 1260, week 19+ = 850-1300.
Air movement at ambient -12 C: week 1 = 70, week 3 = 100, week 6 = 170, week 12 = 340, week 18 = 500, week 19+ = 600-850.
Air movement at ambient -23 C: week 1 = 70, week 3 = 100, week 6 = 170, week 12 = 340, week 18 = 500, week 19+ = 600-680.
Ventilation must remove moisture, remove excessive heat, supply oxygen, remove carbon dioxide, remove dust and dilute aerosolised pathogens.
Place temperature sensors inside the cage; walkway temperature is significantly colder than inside cages, especially in stack-deck belted systems.
Use stir fans when shades are used on open-sided houses; keep shades clean and dust-free to allow air flow.
No tunnel-ventilation air-speed figure is given in this guide.

airQuality.note: Allowable levels of gases at floor level in the house: ammonia (NH3) < 25 ppm, carbon dioxide (CO2) < 5000 ppm, carbon monoxide (CO) < 50 ppm.

heatStress: The guide gives no temperature-humidity thresholds for heat stress; it refers to the 'Understanding Heat Stress in Layers' technical update (English and Telugu) and the 'Best Management Practices During Summer' poster at www.hyline.com.
Anticipate rapid rises in ambient temperature and adjust the diet accordingly; birds eat less when exposed to a rapid temperature increase.
High environmental temperatures depress feed intake; the water:feed ratio (normally 1.5-2.0) increases in high ambient temperatures.
Above the 21-27 C reference range, water consumption may rise to double the table values.
Midnight feeding helps maintain feed consumption in hot climates and may add 2-5 g feed per bird per day.
Use larger particle size mash or crumble to increase intake in hot climates.
Splash cups on drinkers are useful in hot climates.
Avoid direct sunlight on birds with shades or roof overhangs; black shades are preferred.
Energy correction: for each 0.5 C the house is above or below 22 C, subtract or add about 1.8 kcal ME per bird per day.
lighting: Intermittent lighting for chicks is preferred from 0-7 days (can be used up to 14 days): repeating cycle of 4 h light / 2 h dark (16 h light, 8 h dark per 24 h).
If not using intermittent lighting, use 22 h light for 0-3 days and 21 h for 4-7 days (the light-controlled program page says 20 h for 0-7 days). Never use 24 h of light.
Light intensity 30-50 lux during 0-7 days; 25 lux from 8-28 days; 5-15 lux from 29 days through rearing; then 30 lux in lay.
Brooding table light hours: 0-3 d 20 h or intermittent; 4-7 d 20 h or intermittent; 8-14 d 19 h; 15-21 d 17 h; 22-28 d 16 h; 29-35 d 15 h; 36-42 d 14 h.
Light-controlled housing step-down (hours of light by week): wk1 20, wk2 18.5, wk3 17, wk4 15.5, wk5 14, wk6 12.5, wk7-16 11.
Light-controlled housing step-up: wk17 11.5, wk18 12, wk19 13, wk20 14, wk21 15, wk22 16; gradual increases up to 22 weeks, 16 h maximum to end of lay.
Light-controlled housing intensity: 30-50 lux week 1, 25 lux weeks 2-4, 5-15 lux weeks 5-16, 30 lux from ~17 weeks onwards.
Open-sided housing growing period: wk1 20 h, wk2 19, wk3 17, wk4 16, wk5 15, wk6 14, wk7 13, then natural daylight from week 8 until stimulation.

Open-sided housing stimulation: at 16 weeks when BW = 1100 g with 85% uniformity; wk17 +1 h, wk18 +1 h, wk19 +0.5 h, wk20 +0.5 h, wk21 +0.5 h, wk22-24 15-16 h (chart shows 13, 14, 14.5, 15, 15.5, 16 h for weeks 17-22, then 16 h).
Open-sided intensity: 30-50 lux week 1, 25 lux weeks 2-3, 5-15 lux to ~16 weeks, 20-25 lux around transfer (~16-17 weeks), 30 lux in lay.

Begin light stimulation when the flock reaches 1.1 kg body weight with more than 85% uniformity; delay if underweight or poorly uniform; in mixed-age or poorly uniform flocks stimulate on the youngest or lightest pullets.
Light stimulation period should extend into the peaking period.

Light intensity should increase gradually 2 weeks before transfer (not before 14 weeks); final rearing intensity must match the laying-house intensity; match light hours of rearing and laying houses at transfer.
Brighten lights for 3 days after transfer until birds settle.
Measure minimum light intensity at the feeder on bottom-tier cages, midway between lights.
Use warm lights (2700-3500 K) in laying flocks for sufficient red spectrum.
Customised open-sided programs (Hy-Line online tool) hold day length constant with artificial light from 12-17 weeks at the longest natural day length in that window.

Midnight feeding: turn lights on for 1-2 h in the middle of the dark period, at least 3 h of dark before and after; this is in addition to the 16 h day; if removed, reduce gradually at 15 minutes per week; may raise feed intake 2-5 g/bird/day.

feedAndWater: Healthy birds drink 1.5-2.0 times more water than feed; the ratio increases in high ambient temperatures.
Feed and water intakes in the performance tables apply at 21-27 C; above this water intake may double.
Nipple drinkers should deliver a minimum of 60 ml per minute per nipple.

Do not give cold water to chicks; allow flushed water to warm to house temperature. Cup drinkers must be hand-filled for 0-3 days; adjust nipple pressure to leave a hanging drop for 0-3 days and at transfer.
Flush water lines before chick arrival and weekly during rearing and production; test water quality at least once a year, from source and end of line.
Ideal drinking-water pH is 5-7 (table limit 6.3-7.5; below 5 reduces intake and corrodes fittings; above 8 reduces intake and sanitiser effectiveness).

Water quality maxima (ppm or mg/L): nitrate 25, nitrate-N 6, nitrite 4, nitrite-N 1, total dissolved solids 1000 (up to 3000 may not affect performance), chloride 250, sulfate 250, iron <0.3, magnesium 125, potassium 20, sodium 50, manganese 0.05, arsenic 0.5, fluoride 2, aluminium 5, boron 5, cadmium 0.02, cobalt 1, copper 0.6, lead 0.02, mercury 0.003, zinc 1.5.
Water bacteria maxima: total bacteria 1000 CFU/ml, total coliforms 50 CFU/ml, faecal coliforms 0 CFU/ml; ORP 650-750 mEq (range at which 2-4 ppm free chlorine sanitises at pH 5-7).
Water samples: run well 2 minutes before sampling, keep below 10 C, deliver to lab within 24 hours.
Pre-transfer water consumption should be regained within 6 hours of arrival in the laying house; a drop in water consumption is often the first sign of a problem.
Chick body weight should double between arrival and 7 days of age; feed on paper 0-3 days (0-7 days for beak-treated chicks); remove paper at 7-14 days.
Crop fill targets: 75% of chicks with feed in crop at 6 h after placement, 85% at 12 h, 100% at 24 h.

Rearing diet changes are made on body weight, not age: Starter 1 to 180 g, Starter 2 to 410 g, Grower to 920 g, Developer to 1130 g, Pre-Lay for 10-14 days before first egg (not before 15 weeks, not after first egg).
Pullets should enter lay at 1.17-1.20 kg with uniformity above 90%; hit the 6, 12, 18, 24 and 30-week body-weight targets; exceed targets 0-12 weeks but avoid excessive gain after 12 weeks.
Body weight gain from 18-25 weeks should not exceed 20%.
Pre-peaking diet for low intakes (80-85 g/bird/day) begins at 1% production and is fed until average intake reaches 95 g/bird/day.
Layer phases are changed on production and egg size: Layer 1 first egg to peak (typical intake 95 g/day), Layer 2 peak to 90% (100 g/day), Layer 3 89-85% (105 g/day), Layer 4 below 85% (110 g/day).

Rearing diet energy (kcal ME/kg): Starter 1 2950, Starter 2 2850, Grower 2750, Developer 2650, Pre-Lay 2700; crude protein 20.00, 19.00, 17.50, 16.00, 16.50%; calcium 1.05, 1.00, 0.95, 0.90, 2.70%; available P 0.48, 0.47, 0.45, 0.40, 0.45%.

Layer daily intake targets: ME 260-270 kcal/day (Layer 1) and 270-280 kcal/day (Layers 2-4), i.e. 2550-2600 and 2550-2650 kcal/kg; crude protein 16.70, 16.00, 15.30, 14.70 g/day; SID lysine 750, 720, 680, 650 mg/day; sodium and chloride 200 mg/day; linoleic acid 1.60, 1.40, 1.20, 1.00 g/day; choline 180 mg/day.
Calcium g/day and available P mg/day by age: first egg-32 wk 4.10 and 432; 33-55 wk 4.30 and 379; 56-85 wk 4.45 and 352; 86+ wk 4.70 and 329.
Calcium particle size fine(0-2 mm):coarse(2-4 mm) = 100:0 in starter/grower/developer, 50:50 pre-lay, 30:70 from week 17; by age in lay 40:60 (to 32 wk), 35:65 (33-55), 30:70 (56-85), 25:75 (86+).

Feed particle profile (production): <1 mm under 15%, 1-2 mm 20-30%, 2-3 mm 30-40%, >3 mm 10-15%; starter crumble 1-3 mm with under 10% fines; add at least 0.5% liquid oil/fat to mash; leave a 3-4 h gap between mid-day feedings so fines are eaten.
Fibre can be raised to 5-6% from the developer diet to develop crop, gizzard and intestine.

Monitor egg weight every 2 weeks from 21 weeks until 35 weeks, then every 5 weeks; start controlling egg weight when average is within 2 g of target; weigh 100 eggs on the same day within a 3-hour window.
notes: Space guidelines (cages): floor space 40 in2/bird to 6 weeks, 60 in2 from 6-19 weeks, 65 in2 from 19 weeks; nipples 8 birds/nipple to 6 weeks, 5 birds/nipple 6-19 weeks, 4 birds/nipple with access to 2 drinkers in lay; feeder 2.25 in/bird to 6 weeks, 4 in/bird 6-19 weeks, 4 in/bird (environment-controlled) or 5 in/bird (open-sided) in lay.
Uniformity targets (cage): >85% weeks 1-3, >80% weeks 4-12, >85% weeks 13-16, >90% weeks 17-18; 90% uniformity at transfer.
Body-weight monitoring: bulk-weigh 10 boxes of 10 chicks 0-3 weeks; weigh 100 birds individually weekly 4-29 weeks; every 5 weeks 30-90 weeks; weigh birds separately after 3 weeks.
Sera: collect 10-20 samples per flock at 8 weeks, 15 weeks, 16-24 weeks (at least 4 weeks after last inactivated vaccine) and every 10 weeks from 30-80 weeks.

Transfer to laying house by 16 weeks (or after the last live vaccines); if mortality exceeds 0.1% per week perform necropsies; supportive vitamins/probiotics/vitamin C 3 days before and 3 days after transfer; remove sex-slips around 7 weeks and at transfer; shift to growing cages or 60 in2 at 7-13 weeks.

Beak treatment: infrared at hatch or precision trim at 7-10 days (re-trim before 6 weeks or after 12 weeks); cauterise 2 seconds at 650 C (blade variation up to 40 C is common); guide holes 3.56, 4.00, 4.37 mm; vitamin K electrolytes 2 days before and after.
Ideal breast muscle score: ~2 at weeks 1-14, 2 at 14-20, 2-3 at 20-30, 3 after 30 (scale 0-3).
Minimum downtime between flocks 2 weeks; 1 m wide crushed rock or concrete perimeter against rodents.

Vitamin and trace mineral minimums per 1000 kg complete diet (rearing / laying): vitamin A 10,000,000 / 8,000,000 IU; vitamin D3 3,300,000 / 3,300,000 IU; vitamin E 30 / 25 g; vitamin K 3.5 / 3 g; thiamin 2.2 / 2.5 g; riboflavin 6.6 / 5.5 g; niacin 40 / 30 g; pantothenic acid 10 / 10 g; pyridoxine 4.5 / 5 g; biotin 100 / 75 mg; folic acid 1 / 0.9 g; B12 23 / 23 mg; manganese 100 / 100 g; zinc 85 / 80 g; iron 30 / 40 g; copper 15 / 8 g; magnesium 600 / 500 g; iodine 1.5 / 1.2 g; selenium 0.25 / 0.25 g.
Pages skipped as photographs or vaccination/scoring detail: IRBT scoring (pp. 8-11), feed ingredient table (p. 30), feed cost per egg (pp. 31-33).

temperatureC.note: 0-3 d 33-36 C, 4-7 d 30-32 C (cage air temp at chick level); floor temp 35-36 C then 33-35 C
